title: The Day of the Lord and Final Words

verses.text: Now about the times and seasons, brothers, we do not need to write to you.
For you are fully aware that the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.
While people are saying, "Peace and security," destruction will come upon them suddenly, like labor pains on a pregnant woman, and they will not escape.
But you, brothers, are not in the darkness so that this day should overtake you like a thief.
For you are all sons of the light and sons of the day; we do not belong to the night or to the darkness.
So then, let us not sleep as the others do, but let us remain awake and sober.
For those who sleep, sleep at night; and those who get drunk, get drunk at night.
But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and the helmet of our hope of salvation.
For God has not appointed us to suffer wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ.
He died for us so that, whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with Him.
Therefore encourage and build one another up, just as you are already doing.
But we ask you, brothers, to acknowledge those who work diligently among you, who preside over you in the Lord and give you instruction.
In love, hold them in highest regard because of their work. Live in peace with one another.
And we urge you, brothers, to admonish the unruly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.
Make sure that no one repays evil for evil. Always pursue what is good for one another and for all people.
Rejoice at all times.
Pray without ceasing.
Give thanks in every circumstance, for this is God's will for you in Christ Jesus.
Do not extinguish the Spirit.
Do not treat prophecies with contempt,
but test all things. Hold fast to what is good.
Abstain from every form of evil.
Now may the God of peace Himself sanctify you completely, and may your entire spirit, soul, and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
The One who calls you is faithful, and He will do it.
Brothers, pray for us as well.
Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
I charge you before the Lord to have this letter read to all the brothers.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

context.author: Paul, with Silas and Timothy (1:1)
context.genre: Letter of encouragement, warm and personal
context.audience: The church in Thessalonica, a young church under pressure
context.setting: Paul turns to the timing of the day of the Lord, telling the Thessalonians it will come like a thief but that they are children of the day. He then gives a series of brief commands: respect leaders, live in peace, rejoice always, pray continually, give thanks, and test everything.
context.custom: “Peace and security” (v.3) was a slogan of the Roman empire, and Paul says sudden destruction will come on those who trust in it. “Breastplate of faith and love” and “helmet of hope” (v.8) are soldier images.
context.timelineImmediate: The letter ends. Paul wrote a second letter soon after to answer new questions.
context.timelineBible: “The day of the Lord” is a major prophetic theme (Amos 5:18-20; Joel 2; Zephaniah 1). The image of a thief appears in Jesus’ teaching (Matthew 24:43).
context.sparkNotes: The day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night. When people say, “Peace and security,” sudden destruction will come. But you are children of the light, so stay awake and sober, wearing faith, love, and hope. Respect your leaders, be at peace, warn the idle, encourage the fainthearted. Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances, and test everything.

translation.meaning: To examine like a metal assayer, and keep what is genuine.
Without a gap, like a hacking cough that keeps coming back.

otBackground.note: The day of the Lord will be darkness.
They say peace when there is no peace.

overview.summary: The day of the Lord comes suddenly, but believers are children of the day. Paul ends with short commands: rejoice, pray, give thanks, and test everything.
overview.settingLine: Paul writes from Corinth to the young church in Thessalonica.

history.t: Rome presented its rule as bringing peace. Scholars disagree about “peace and security” in 5:3. Some hear Roman propaganda, while others hear the prophets’ warnings against false peace (Jeremiah 6:14; Ezekiel 13:10) and doubt it was a fixed Roman slogan.

Paul tells them not to “quench the Spirit” or “treat prophecies with contempt,” and to “test all things” (5:19-21). Prophecy was a gift of the Spirit in his churches (1 Corinthians 14), and what was said was to be weighed.

customs.t: “The day of the Lord will come just like a thief in the night” (5:2). Jesus used the same picture (Matthew 24:43; Luke 12:39). A thief gives no warning, so Paul tells believers to stay awake and sober (5:6).

Paul ends with “greet all the brothers with a holy kiss” (5:26), and says the same in Romans 16:16 and 1 Corinthians 16:20. A kiss was an ordinary greeting among family and friends, and the church made it a sign of its shared family life.

archaeology.h: Peace in Stone: the Ara Pacis
archaeology.t: The Ara Pacis Augustae, the Altar of Augustan Peace, was dedicated in Rome in 9 BC. Its carvings of a peaceful, fruitful empire are some of the best surviving examples of Roman peace imagery.

Paul pictures faith and love as a breastplate and the hope of salvation as a helmet (5:8). Segmented plate armor came into use in his time, and a Roman cavalry helmet of the 1st century AD was found at Hallaton in England. Isaiah 59:17 has the same picture of God as a warrior.

overview.discussion: Paul says “give thanks in all circumstances.” What is one situation where gratitude feels hard, and what is one small thing in it I could still thank God for?
overview.book: The first letter to the Thessalonians · 5 chapters. One of Paul’s earliest letters, full of warmth and hope.
overview.author: Paul

historicalImage.caption: The Last Judgment, by Michelangelo (1536-41), in the Sistine Chapel. First Thessalonians 5:2 says the day of the Lord comes "like a thief in the night," and 2 Thessalonians 1:7-10 pictures the Lord Jesus revealed from heaven. Michelangelo's scene blends many biblical passages.
